security_audit.summary: No prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or covert command execution was found in the reviewed WordPress orchestrator files. Most static findings are documentation examples for URLs, Claude skill paths, local temporary paths, .env handling, and Markdown code fences. The confirmed risks are operational: an unsigned remote WP-CLI download and temporary WordPress database dump handling that should be tightened before publication.

remediation.issue: The install guide downloads WP-CLI PHAR from raw GitHub and installs it without verification.
remediation.suggestion: Use an official pinned release and verify checksum or signature before making the binary executable.

remediation.issue: The workflow writes a WordPress database dump to /tmp and copies it into the project directory.
remediation.suggestion: Store database dumps in a restricted path, document cleanup steps, and warn users not to commit or share the dump.

remediation.issue: Absolute /root/.claude and ~/.claude paths reduce portability and can look like hidden file access.
remediation.suggestion: Document these as user-approved installation paths and prefer variables or relative skill references where possible.

remediation.issue: Frontend examples include third-party CDN URLs for development assets.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend pinned, bundled, or integrity-checked assets for production themes.

content.user_title: Coordinate WordPress Site Builds and Audits
content.value_statement: WordPress projects require setup, audits, SEO, testing, and handoff across several tools. This skill coordinates those phases and calls related WordPress skills.
actual_capabilities: Runs a structured discovery interview for WordPress requirements, branding, SEO goals, and handoff needs.
Builds phased todo lists for setup, content, SEO, performance, security, visual QA, and launch tasks.
Coordinates companion skills for Docker setup, SEO audits, visual QA, performance checks, and white-label admin work.
Defines workflows for wp-setup, wp-audit, and wp-launch style project commands.
Documents theme packaging, GitHub deployment, WP Pusher setup, production sync, and client handoff steps.
limitations: Requires companion WordPress skills and local tools for many scripted workflows.
Needs user-approved credentials, URLs, hosting access, and repository access before deployment tasks.
Does not replace manual review for security, legal text, content quality, or production change control.
Example paths and domains must be adapted before use in a real project.

use_cases.title: Plan a New WordPress Site
use_cases.description: Gather business goals, brand assets, pages, integrations, SEO targets, and handoff needs before setup starts.

use_cases.title: Audit an Existing Site
use_cases.description: Coordinate SEO, visual QA, performance, security, and content checks into a prioritized action plan.

use_cases.title: Prepare Client Handoff
use_cases.description: Package the theme, verify launch readiness, configure admin branding, and prepare clear client documentation.

prompt_templates.title: Start Project Discovery
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a new site build.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use wp-orchestrator to interview me for a new WordPress site. Focus on business goals, pages, branding, SEO, and handoff needs.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Setup Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Turn discovery answers into an implementation plan.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use wp-orchestrator to create a phased setup plan for my WordPress project. Include Docker setup, theme tasks, plugins, SEO, QA, and launch steps.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Site Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Use wp-orchestrator to audit this WordPress site: [site URL]. Coordinate SEO, visual QA, performance, security, and handoff findings into one report.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Production Launch
prompt_templates.prompt: Use wp-orchestrator to prepare this WordPress project for launch. Verify packaging, repository deployment, production sync, admin branding, documentation, and client handoff.

output_examples.input: Set up a WordPress site for a local service business.
output_examples.output: A discovery checklist, plugin plan, Docker setup sequence, theme task list, SEO checklist, and launch readiness plan.

output_examples.input: Audit my staging WordPress site before launch.
output_examples.output: A consolidated audit report with prioritized SEO, visual, performance, security, content, and handoff recommendations.

output_examples.input: Prepare a client handoff for a finished theme.
output_examples.output: A launch checklist, packaging steps, deployment guidance, admin training outline, and client documentation topics.

best_practices: Run discovery before setup so requirements, brand assets, and handoff expectations are documented.
Confirm commands, credentials, domains, and deployment targets before running shell or production tasks.
Use the audit output to create prioritized todos with owners, severity, and launch impact.
anti_patterns: Do not run production sync or database commands without verified backups and approval.
Do not use placeholder domains, paths, or credentials in a live project.
Do not treat automated audit results as a substitute for manual launch review.

faq.question: What does this skill coordinate?
faq.answer: It coordinates WordPress discovery, setup, auditing, testing, packaging, deployment, and client handoff workflows.

faq.question: Does it create a complete WordPress site by itself?
faq.answer: No. It guides and coordinates tasks, often using companion skills and local development tools.

faq.question: Can it audit an existing site?
faq.answer: Yes. It can organize SEO, visual QA, performance, security, and content checks into one action plan.

faq.question: Does it require shell access?
faq.answer: Many workflows use shell, Docker, WP-CLI, Git, or local scripts, so commands should be reviewed before execution.

faq.question: Is it suitable for client handoff work?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes launch checks, white-label admin guidance, documentation topics, and training preparation.

faq.question: Which tools does it support?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
